language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hello, my name is King Toot, and like my father and his father, I am building a pyramid.
However, I don't want my pyramid to be as "square" as theirs.
I am working with my architects to come up with a design.
My requirement is that the base must have at least three sides and must be self contained.
The first architect recommeds a pentagon for the base of the pyramid. It has 5 sides that are of equal length.
The second architect is more ambitious and recommeds an octagon. It has 8 sides that are of equal length.
The final architect recommeds a trapezium. It has 4 sides like a square,
but it only has one pair of parallel lines and the sides do not need to be of equal length.
All three recommendations have at least three sides and are self contained. They are all polygons.
What do you think we should build? Let's get started!
